items.title: Osun Council chairmen, soldiers in standoff over illegal mining crackdown
items.description: By Shina Abubakar OSOGBO — Tension erupted on Tuesday at Ibodi in Atakunmosa West Local Government Area of Osun State as council chairmen from the Ijesa South Federal Constituency and military personnel had a confrontation during an enforcement operation against alleged illegal mining activities. The council chairmen, accompanied by operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and the Nigeria Police Force, said they were responding to complaints from residents over environmental degradation and security concerns linked to illegal mining. According to the chairmen, the confrontation occurred when members of the enforcement team attempted to halt the collection of levies and the issuance of tickets at a mining site. They alleged that military personnel at the location prevented the operation, resulting in a standoff. The situation was later brought under control following the intervention of the member representing Ijesa South Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Sanya Omirin, and senior police officers, after which the enforcement team proceeded with its activities. The delegation later visited Ijana Wasare community, where it announced the closure of what it described as illegal mining sites and directed that the issuance of tickets to unlicensed miners should cease. Addressing journalists after the exercise, the Chairman of Ilesa West Local Government, Mr. Lanre Balogun, who spoke on behalf of the council chairmen in the constituency, said the operation was aimed at addressing the environmental and security challenges associated with illegal mining. He said communities including Iperindo, Itagunmodi, Igangan, Itapa and Odogbo had been affected by environmental degradation, destruction of farmlands, pollution of water sources and other challenges allegedly linked to illegal artisanal mining. Balogun said the local government authorities had sought information from the Osun State Mining Office on operators in the area, adding that the response did not resolve their concerns. He further alleged that some mining sites were operating without the necessary licences and that unauthorised persons were collecting revenue through ticketing at the sites. According to him, the council chairmen subsequently invited the NSCDC to inspect the affected communities and commended the agency for its response. The chairmen also met with the Owa Sare of Ijana Wasare, Oba Adeniyi Adedeji, and other traditional rulers and stakeholders, where they agreed to collaborate in addressing illegal mining activities. They said their intervention was based on the constitutional responsibilities of local governments regarding environmental protection and community development. Speaking during the inspection, Hon. Omirin alleged that the Osun State Government was permitting illegal mining activities through the issuance of tickets to operators without valid mining licences. He maintained that the Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development is the authority responsible for issuing mining licences and said he would raise the matter at the National Assembly. The council chairmen announced an immediate ban on illegal mining operations and the issuance of tickets in the affected communities, directing operators to obtain the appropriate licences from the Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development before resuming operations. items.title: Osun Election: CSOs urge parties to uphold democratic values
items.description: By Shina Abubakar OSOGBO — A coalition of civil society organisations under the aegis of the Partnership for Ethical Governance has called on political parties participating in the August 15 Osun State governorship election to demonstrate political maturity and uphold democratic values. Speaking on behalf of the coalition, its Chairman, Comrade Debo Adeniran, expressed concern over what he described as rising incidents of politically motivated violence, intimidation and attacks ahead of the poll, warning that such developments could undermine public confidence in the electoral process. He stressed that elections should not be treated as warfare, noting that political opponents should not be regarded as enemies. According to him, democracy guarantees citizens the freedom to choose their leaders without fear, intimidation, coercion or violence. “The essence of democracy is to give the people the freedom to choose their leaders without fear, intimidation, coercion or violence. Elections are not wars. Political opponents are not enemies. Victory at the polls must never come at the cost of human misery, trauma and loss of lives,” he said. Adeniran noted that electoral violence discourages voter participation, weakens public confidence in democratic institutions and leaves lasting consequences for communities. The coalition urged eligible voters across Osun State to participate peacefully in the August 15 governorship election, assuring that democracy is strengthened when citizens freely express their choices through the ballot box. It also called on the leadership of the Accord Party, All Progressives Congress (APC), African Democratic Congress (ADC), All Progressives Movement (APM) and other participating political parties to consistently preach restraint to their supporters before, during and after the election. According to the coalition, party leaders should reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and ensure that any grievances arising from the election are addressed through lawful and constitutional means. It further cautioned politicians against inciting youths to engage in electoral violence, stressing that those who sponsor violence often do not bear its consequences, while young people and communities suffer the most. items.title: Customs, agents disagree over National Single Window operations
items.description: By Godwin Oritse & Efe Onodjae There are indications of festering disagreements over the implementation of the National Single Window (NSW), a centralized digital portal launched by the Federal Government in March this year to address delays in import-export processing at the ports. It allows importers and exporters to submit trade documents once, replacing duplicate paperwork across multiple agencies. President of the National Council of Managing Directors of Licensed Customs Agents (NCMDLCA), Lucky Amiwero, told Vanguard that the system is not operating as envisaged, urging the government to hand over the implementation to the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS). But Customs itself is saying there is no problem with the system presently, adding that it has recorded some early successes. However, Amiwero said the current arrangement has failed to simplify trade documentation and cargo clearance, contrary to the objectives of a Single Window system. “Instead of a single window, what we have are multiple windows that are complicating the process for importers and clearing agents,” he said. He dismissed reports that the project had entered a second phase, insisting that challenges identified during the initial phase remained unresolved. According to him, the NCS has the legal mandate, operational platform and technical expertise required to implement the project under the Customs Act. Amiwero also disagreed with the plans for electronic transmission of cargo manifests outside the Customs framework, insisting that manifest administration is a statutory responsibility of the NCS. He urged the government to harmonise all trade documentation on a single Customs platform instead of creating multiple systems that duplicate functions. The freight forwarder further expressed concern over persistent cargo clearance delays, saying they continue to increase demurrage and other port charges borne by importers. Meanwhile, the NCS has said that the NSW platform has enhanced trade facilitation, improved efficiency in goods clearing and Nigeria’s competitiveness in international trade. Also the Customs, in collaboration with the National Single Window (NSW) Secretariat, has commenced stakeholder sensitisation on submission of electronic vessel manifest as implementation of the next phase of the NSW gathers momentum. Addressing the stakeholders, Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of ICT/Modernisation, Oluyomi Adebakin, said the exercise builds on consultations held before and after the launch of Phase One of the NSW on March 27, 2026. She described the NSW platform as a globally accepted trade facilitation tool that would improve efficiency, transparency and Nigeria’s competitiveness in international trade. “Since the introduction of the National Single Window, the country has begun to experience its benefits. Nigeria’s standing in international trade is improving,” she said. Adebakin stressed that electronic manifest submission would not alter Customs’ statutory responsibilities but would simply provide a faster and more transparent method of processing documents. She added that the platform would enhance trade facilitation, improve data integrity and strengthen anti-smuggling efforts. National Coordinator of the National Single Window Project, Tola Fakolade, commended the NCS for supporting implementation of the initiative. He disclosed that the platform has so far issued over 100,000 licences and permits while registering more than 1,000 users, describing the progress as a significant milestone in Nigeria’s trade modernisation programme. items.title: Suspect among 7 dead in Thailand school shooting; 15 injured
items.description: At least seven people were killed on Friday when a student opened fire at a school in Thailand before turning the gun on himself, a national police official said. Students streamed out of the Debsirin Nonthaburi School, on the northwestern outskirts of Bangkok, as the wounded were loaded onto ambulances and teachers hugged each other and cried. In photos circulated by emergency workers, one person is seen lying down on a stretcher outside an ambulance, while another is attended to by a medic. Lt. Col. Trirong Phophan, a spokesman for the National Police, told Reuters the suspected shooter was among the seven people killed. Fifteen people were injured, he added. One 18-year-old student told Reuters he initially thought there were firecrackers going off or someone banging an object. “I didn’t think it was a gun at first,” he said. “There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again.” “It’s such a terrible incident. It should never have happened. How could this happen in our country?” Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters at Bangkok’s Government House. Second school shooting Education Minister Prasert Jantararuangtong told Reuters that both teachers and students were among those reported dead. Police identified the perpetrator as a student. It is the second school shooting in Thailand this year after a teacher died and a student was injured in the south of the country in February . Emergency worker Kiatikhun Verapongpradith, 47, described arriving as the shooting was ongoing and his team treated students with injuries in the back, chest and arms. They found a male teacher lying dead on an upper floor of the school, and in another room they found a female teacher with wounds in her chest and arm. “We gave CPR for about 30 minutes and rushed her to the hospital as we could not get her heart rate up, but we tried our best,” he said. Traffic near the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Nonthaburi was nearly at a standstill, an AFP journalist saw, with local media reporting that parents were picking up their children following the incident. In the 2025 academic year, the school had an enrollment of around 3,100 students and 147 teachers, according to district authorities. Deputy Education Minister Akkharanan Kannakittinan said in a statement he was coordinating to provide assistance. History of shootings Gun ownership and gun violence are not uncommon in Thailand, which has seen a series of deadly shootings in the past six years, with children among the victims. Thailand’s worst mass killing by a single perpetrator in its recent history took place in 2022, when a former policeman ran amok in a three-hour gun-and-knife attack in the northeast that killed 36 people , including 22 children stabbed as they slept at a daycare centre. A gunman killed five people , including security guards and a vendor, at a Bangkok market in July 2025 before turning the gun on himself, while a teacher died in the southern city of Hat Yai in February this year when a shooter opened fire at a school where she worked. In 2020, a soldier killed 29 people in a shooting rampage in Nakhon Ratchasima. And in 2023, a 14-year-old used a modified handgun to kill two people and wound five others at a luxury Bangkok shopping centre.

items.title: La hausse de la température marine impactera l’économie en Tunisie
items.description: En juillet 2026, les températures marines dans le golfe de Gabès ont dépassé les 30 °C avec des pics atteignant environ 34 °C, menaçant la pêche et les écosystèmes côtiers d’une région qui concentre 23 % de la capacité d’hébergement touristique du pays, notamment dans les zones de Djerba et Zarzis. La menace concerne les deux principales activités économiques de la région du sud-est tunisien: la pêche et le tourisme, déjà très affectés par la pollution industrielle. Latif Belhedi Cette hausse des températures marines, phénomène marin distinct des températures de l’air ambiant, témoigne d’un important stress écologique. Si les activités touristiques immédiates ne sont pas affectées, ce réchauffement menace la viabilité à long terme de la pêche et de la biodiversité côtière. Réchauffement marin exceptionnel en Méditerranée Cette situation s’inscrit dans une crise régionale plus vaste. Au 1 er août 2026, la température moyenne de surface de la mer dans le bassin méditerranéen s’élevait à 27,3 °C. Les données indiquent qu’à cette date, environ 65,8 % de la Méditerranée subissait des conditions de canicule marine. Les tendances mondiales reflètent cette hausse régionale : la température moyenne de surface de la mer hors zones polaires a atteint 20,86 °C en juin 2026, soit le niveau le plus élevé jamais enregistré officiellement pour un mois de juin. Bien que les prévisions pour le 1 er août aient laissé entrevoir une diminution de l’étendue et de l’intensité de la canicule, des conditions modérées à fortes ont persisté dans plusieurs secteurs. Une analyse des données historiques révèle une baisse de 44 % de la productivité de la pêche dans le golfe de Gabès entre 2000 et 2015. La vague de chaleur de 2026 aggrave ces facteurs de stress existants, exerçant une pression supplémentaire sur un écosystème déjà fragilisé. Exposition économique : tourisme et pêche Les enjeux économiques pour le sud de la Tunisie sont considérables. Le corridor Djerba-Zarzis-Gabès constitue un moteur essentiel de l’industrie touristique nationale. En 2023, la capacité d’hébergement de la région s’élevait à 150 établissements et 53 114 lits, soit environ 23 % du total des 230 726 lits touristiques que comptait à cette date la Tunisie. Le tourisme côtier et la pêche soutiennent, ensemble, environ 450 000 emplois à l’échelle nationale. Et l’économie bleue tunisienne a contribué à près de 14 % de la production économique nationale en 2018. Pr ailleurs, plus de 66 % de la population (environ 7,6 millions de personnes) réside dans les zones côtières. Ce qui donne une idée des impacts attendus du réchauffement climatique sur l’économie tunisienne en général et sur celle du Golfe de Gabès en particulier. Avec Nomad . L’article La hausse de la température marine impactera l’économie en Tunisie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Firms expect borrowing cost to decline in 3 months
items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Firms are expecting borrowing cost for banks’ loans to decline in the next three months deapite seeing rates elevated in July. This was contained in the Central Bank of Nigeria’s, CBN, latest Business Expectation Survey Report. CBN said: “Respondents expect borrowing rates to remain elevated across the same periods, as indicated by the consistently positive borrowing rate indices. “The relatively stable indices, fluctuating around 18-19 points, suggest expectations of a marginal decrease in borrowing costs over the near – to medium term.” The survey report also showed that the Business Confidence Index was 5.7 points, reflecting continued optimistic sentiment among formal businesses on the macro economy. According to CBN, Respondents’ positive sentiment on macro economy was largely underpinned by increased demand (22.3 percent ), economic diversification (21.4 percent) and access to finance (15 percent ), while more guarded views were primarily driven by inflation (27.7 percent), insecurity (22.4 percent) ongoing energy-related challenges (23.4 percent) and elevated geopolitical uncertainties (16.5 percent). The outlook over the next six months, CBN maintained remains strong, with confidence indices in all sectors reflecting positive sentiment over the review periods. During the review period, businesses identified high/multiple taxation (70.8), insecurity (69.7) and high interest rate (66.3) as the top three business constraints. These were followed by unfavourable political climate (62.2) and high bank charges (62.0). But competition (61.1) and unclear Economic Laws (58.4) ranked lower but remain significant. CBN noted that at the bottom of the top ten constraints were financial constraints (56.6) and poor infrastructure (55.1) reflecting relatively lower, though still significant factors. On expansion outlook, the electricity, water and gas sector posted the highest expansion outlook at 85.7 index points. Nonetheless, employment expectations in August 2026 were mostly cautious across sectors, with the Mining & Quarrying sector having the most optimistic hiring outlook. items.title: Manasseh Awuni invokes RTI for evidence of Sedina Tamakloe’s appeal filing timelines
items.description: Investigative journalist and coordinator of the civil society-led Pledge Against Corruption campaign, Manasseh Azure Awuni, has filed a right to information (RTI) request to the Judicial Service, asking for detailed timelines of Sedina Christine Tamakloe Attionu’s appeal. Sedina Tamakloe, the Chief Executive of the state-owned Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) from November 2013 to January 2017, was acquitted and discharged by the Court of Appeal on July 30, 2026. She was convicted and sentenced to 10 years in prison by the High Court (Financial Crimes Division) on April 16, 2024, after a trial in absentia. She had failed to return to Ghana after the court granted her permission to seek medical care in the United States. She had been charged with seventy-eight counts of Conspiracy to Steal, Stealing, Conspiracy to Willfully Cause Financial Loss to the State, Willfully Causing Financial Loss to the State, Causing Loss to Public Property, Improper Payment of Public Funds, Money Laundering, Unauthorised Commitment Resulting in Financial Obligation for the Government and Contravention of the Public Procurement Act. On May 9, 2024, while she was still at large, court records indicate that Sedina challenged her conviction at the Court of Appeal, which acquitted her after she was repatriated from the United States in June 2026 to serve her sentence. While the Court of Appeal judgment has generally been received as sound, doubts still linger in the minds of a section of Ghanaians about the timelines of her appeal. Though the Appeal was said to have been filed in May 2024, the Attorney-General’s Department is said to have been notified only in February 2026, fueling conspiracy theories about possible underhanded dealings. The Attorney-General and Minister of Justice from 2021 to January 2025, Godfred Yeboah Dame, said in a press statement that he had not heard about Sedina’s appeal at the time he left office. Manasseh’s RTI request of the Judicial Service seeks to lay the matter to rest. It seeks an explanation of the nearly two-year delay in notifying the Attorney-General’s office of the appeal, as well as key evidence of the filing timelines. Manasseh requested the following information from the Judicial Service: 1. The date and time Suit Number H2/17/2026 (Sedina Christine Tamakloe Attionu Vs. The Republic) was filed. (Attach Form 2 and Form 6 of the processes relating to this case) 2. The date and time the suit above was served on the Office of the Attorney-General. (Please attach proof/affidavit of service indicating when the appeal was served on the Attorney-General) 3. Photocopies of receipts of payment of bonds, as well as all receipts of payment made by the appellant for any other processes in this case. 4. The date and time the suit in question was recorded in the court’s Case Registration Book. (Please attach a photocopy—or a printout, if cases are listed electronically—of the page of the Case Registration Book on which the above suit was listed, showing its position among other cases filed before and after the suit in question. If this case was listed on a fresh page, please provide a photocopy of the preceding page.) 5. The BP Number of the Suit Number H2/17/2026. 6. If the information in the public domain that the Attorney-General was not notified of the appeal purportedly filed in May 2024 until February 2026 is true, please provide an explanation for this. Is this a norm or an anomaly? And what occasioned the delay in serving the Attorney General? According to Manasseh, the RTI request, which was submitted to the Judicial Service on August 5, 2026, “is in line with my work as a journalist and a quest for transparency, which would help to deepen trust in the judiciary.”

items.title: Manufacturers’ confidence rebounds despite high borrowing costs, power woes
items.description: By Yinka Kolawole Manufacturers’ confidence in Nigeria’s business environment rebounded in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2’26) buoyed by expectations of improved government policies and a more favourable operating climate. But the sector operators have continued to grapple with high borrowing costs, inadequate power supply, foreign exchange constraints and multiple taxation. The latest Manufacturers CEO Confidence Index (MCCI) released by the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, MAN, showed that the aggregate index rose to 52.1 points in Q2 2026, up from 48.7 points in the first quarter (Q1’26) indicating a return to positive business sentiment. Director General of MAN, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, said the improvement reflected manufacturers’ optimism about the direction of government reforms rather than any significant improvement in current operating conditions. He stated: “The increase in the MCCI to 52.1 points signals renewed confidence among manufacturers, driven largely by expectations that recent policy initiatives, including the Nigeria Industrial Policy, the ‘Nigeria First’ Policy, Executive Orders 003 and 005, and the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, will improve the operating environment.” He, however, noted that the optimism remained fragile as manufacturers continued to face severe operational challenges. “The confidence expressed by manufacturers is largely forward-looking. Actual business and employment conditions during the second quarter remained weak, with both indicators still below the 50-point threshold, reflecting subdued business activity,” Ajayi-Kadir stated. He listed limited access to finance, persistent electricity shortages, high production costs, inadequate foreign exchange availability, weak consumer demand and multiple taxation as the major constraints confronting manufacturers. Ajayi-Kadir said manufacturers remained dissatisfied with the high cost of bank credit, attributing it to the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Monetary Policy Rate, MPR, of 26.5 per cent. “Commercial lending rates remain prohibitively high for manufacturers. The current monetary policy stance continues to constrain access to affordable financing needed for investment and expansion,” he said. The MAN DG further expressed concern over continued regulatory bottlenecks and uncertainty surrounding the implementation of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, saying manufacturers were yet to enjoy the full benefits of the reforms aimed at reducing multiple taxation and easing regulatory burdens. Ajayi-Kadir added that although local sourcing of raw materials had improved, government ministries, departments and agencies were yet to substantially increase patronage of Made-in-Nigeria products as envisaged under the “Nigeria First” policy. He urged the Federal Government to ensure strict compliance with the directive requiring MDAs to source at least 80 per cent of their procurement locally, while calling on the CBN to reduce the MPR to below 20 per cent and prioritise foreign exchange allocation to manufacturers to stimulate production and accelerate industrial growth. items.title: Andy Dosty becomes first Ghanaian DJ to headline SummerStage
items.description: Ghanaian radio personality and DJ Andy Dosty has become the first Ghanaian DJ to headline New York’s Capital One City Parks Foundation SummerStage Festival. Andy Dosty, born Andrew Amoh, represented Ghana at this year’s edition of the globally celebrated festival, delivering a performance that showcased Ghanaian music on one of New York’s most iconic outdoor stages. As part of the festival’s 40th anniversary celebrations, Andy Dosty was not only the only Ghanaian DJ on the line-up but also the first Ghanaian DJ to headline the event, making his appearance a landmark moment for Ghana’s entertainment industry and a significant milestone in the global recognition of Ghanaian DJs. Known for his energy behind the turntables, Andy Dosty thrilled festival-goers with a set featuring back-to-back Ghanaian hits. His performance captivated the audience, with many fans singing along, dancing and embracing the sounds of Ghana throughout his set. The internationally acclaimed SummerStage Festival featured a line-up of celebrated musicians, DJs and live bands from around the world. Andy Dosty’s inclusion on the platform reflects his growing international recognition and his continued efforts to promote Ghanaian music beyond the country’s borders. Over the years, Andy Dosty has established himself as one of Ghana’s respected media personalities. Beyond entertaining audiences, he has consistently used his platforms to discover, support and promote both established and emerging Ghanaian artistes, making him one of the country’s influential voices in music and entertainment. An award-winning broadcaster, DJ and producer, Andy Dosty has collaborated with some of Ghana’s biggest music stars, including KiDi, E.L, Ras Kuuku, Okyeame Kwame and many others, contributing to the promotion and growth of Ghana’s music industry. He currently hosts The Afternoon Ride on Hitz FM 103.9 FM, airing Monday to Thursday from 12:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m., where he combines music, entertainment news, celebrity interviews and discussions with listeners. In addition, he hosts The Library on Joy FM 99.7 FM every Friday from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. The programme has become a favourite among music lovers for its concept, taking listeners behind the scenes of hit songs by exploring the songwriting process, production journey, inspiration and stories behind some of Ghana’s biggest records. Andy Dosty’s appearance at the 2026 Capital One City Parks Foundation SummerStage Festival marks another international milestone in his career. His achievement as the first Ghanaian DJ to headline the festival highlights his personal accomplishments while shining a global spotlight on Ghana’s music industry. It also reinforces his commitment to promoting Ghanaian music and culture on the international stage while opening doors for future generations of Ghanaian DJs.

items.title: Crise de Ceuta : de la Chine à la Colombie, l’ombre du Mossad et de Rabat plane
items.description: Couvert de honte par la fuite collective de sa jeunesse vers l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta le jour de la “fête du trône”, le Maroc a tenté d’accuser l’Algérie. Mais les preuves qui se sont accumulées ne laissent guère de doute quant à une opération orchestrée par les services marocains eux-mêmes, avec l’aide de leurs alliés. Les services de renseignements et les analystes chinois en sont convaincus. Pour eux, l'assaut sur Ceuta s’inscrit dans une opération de renseignement orchestrée par le Maroc et Israël pour déstabiliser l'Espagne. D’autres pays le pensent aussi. Crise de Ceuta : les interrogations des services chinois sur l’implication du Mossad Dans un article publié cette semaine par Modern Diplomacy , revue internationale spécialisée en géopolitique, et repris par le journal espagnol El Mundo , la politologue égyptienne Nadia Helmy, spécialiste de la politique chinoise et des relations sino-israéliennes, a ouvertement soutenu cette théorie. Elle a écrit que certains rapports établis à Pékin interprètent ce qui s’est passé à Ceuta comme une opération de guerre hybride visant à accroître la pression sur le gouvernement de Pedro Sánchez. La manœuvre aurait impliqué le Mossad, qui chercherait à mener une campagne de déstabilisation contre l'Espagne. “Les centres d'analyse des services de renseignement chinois ont examiné l'escalade des tensions diplomatiques et politiques entre l'Espagne et Israël. Dans cette perspective, la détérioration des relations bilatérales pourrait avoir incité le Mossad à s'impliquer dans la crise migratoire entre le Maroc et l'Espagne, aggravant ainsi la situation et infiltrant des agents pour semer le mécontentement et le chaos au sein de la population marocaine”, explique la spécialiste. Dans des conversations privées, certains diplomates et analystes proches des cercles politiques de Pékin se demandent également si l'attaque contre Ceuta a un lien quelconque avec la détérioration progressive des relations entre Madrid et Tel-Aviv, marquée par les critiques du gouvernement espagnol concernant le massacre de Gaza et la reconnaissance de l'État palestinien, écrit El Mundo. Comme le rappelle un diplomate dans le même journal, “depuis la normalisation des relations en 2020, le Maroc et Israël sont devenus des alliés et ont renforcé leur coopération en matière de défense et de renseignement”. Gustavo Petro : Le Maroc “a cédé aux desseins d'un génocidaire en fuite” Les images de milliers de personnes franchissant la frontière espagnole ont aussi suscité un mélange d'étonnement et d'incrédulité chez de nombreux internautes chinois qui se demandent “comment est-il possible qu'ils traversent la frontière si facilement ?”. Et il n’y a pas qu’en Chine que le Maroc et Israël sont pointés du doigt. L’ancien président colombien Gustavo Petro a directement accusé le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahou d'être le principal responsable de l’assaut sur Ceuta. Petro a assuré que Netanyahou “paye les pauvres pour qu'ils risquent leur vie afin de rejoindre l'Espagne” et que le Maroc “a cédé aux desseins d'un génocidaire en fuite”. Pour le président colombien, Israël mène des campagnes de déstabilisation contre les gouvernements qui critiquent sa politique au Moyen-Orient. L’article Crise de Ceuta : de la Chine à la Colombie, l’ombre du Mossad et de Rabat plane est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Seven dead, including gunman, at Thailand school shooting
items.description: At least seven people were killed on Friday ‌when a student opened fire at a school in Thailand before turning the gun on himself, a national police official said. Students streamed out of the Debsirin Nonthaburi School, on the northwestern outskirts of Bangkok, as the wounded were loaded on to ambulances and teachers hugged each other and cried. In photos circulated by ​emergency workers, one person is seen lying down on a stretcher outside an ambulance, while another is attended to by ​a medic. One 18-year-old student told Reuters he initially thought there were firecrackers going off or someone banging ⁠an object. “I didn’t think it was a gun at first,” he said. “There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. ​Then it started again.” Lt. Col. Trirong Phophan, a spokesman for the National Police, told Reuters the suspected shooter was among the seven people killed. ​Fifteen people were injured, he added. SECOND SCHOOL SHOOTING Education Minister Prasert Jantararuangtong told Reuters that both teachers and students were among those reported dead. Police identified the perpetrator as a student. It is the second school shooting in Thailand this year after a teacher died and a student was injured in the south of the ​country in February. Emergency worker Kiatikhun Verapongpradith, 47, described arriving as the shooting was ongoing and his team treated students with injuries in ​the back, chest and arms. They found a male teacher lying dead on an upper floor of the school, and in another room they found ‌a female ⁠teacher with wounds in her chest and arm. “We gave CPR for about 30 minutes and rushed her to the hospital as we could not get her heart rate up, but we tried our best,” he said. In the 2025 academic year, the school had an enrollment of around 3,100 students and 147 teachers, according to district authorities. Deputy Education Minister Akkharanan Kannakittinan said in a statement he was coordinating to provide ​assistance. HISTORY OF SHOOTINGS Gun ownership and gun ​violence are not uncommon in ⁠Thailand, which has seen a series of deadly shootings in the past six years, with children among the victims. Thailand’s worst mass killing by a single perpetrator in its recent history took place in 2022, ​when a former policeman ran amok in a three-hour gun-and-knife attack in the northeast that killed 36 people ​including 22 children ⁠stabbed as they slept at a daycare centre . A gunman killed five people, including security guards and a vendor, at a Bangkok market in July 2025 before turning the gun on himself, while a teacher died in the southern city of Hat Yai in February this year when a shooter ⁠opened fire ​at a school where she worked. In 2020, a soldier killed 29 people ​in a shooting rampage in Nakhon Ratchasima. And in 2023, a 14-year-old used a modified handgun to kill two people and wound five others at a luxury Bangkok shopping centre .

items.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, August 7, 2026
items.description: The naira remained relatively stable against the United States dollar across both the official and parallel foreign exchange markets as traders monitored liquidity conditions and demand pressures. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the official exchange rate stood at about ₦1,368.22 per dollar, according to figures published by the Central Bank of Nigeria and market data aggregators. The rate is derived from the volume-weighted average of completed transactions in the official market. The latest available CBN exchange-rate data also shows the official market trading within a narrow band around the ₦1,36x range in recent sessions, indicating limited volatility in the formal market. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the dollar traded at around ₦1,405 per dollar on Friday, reflecting a premium of roughly ₦37 above the official NFEM rate. The gap between the two markets remains significantly lower than the wide disparities recorded in 2024 and parts of 2025, suggesting some improvement in price convergence following ongoing foreign-exchange reforms. Currency dealers said demand from importers, travellers, and other retail users continued to support the parallel-market rate, while supply from exporters and autonomous sources helped keep the official market relatively stable. Analysts noted that movements in external reserves, foreign portfolio inflows, and crude-oil receipts will remain key factors influencing the naira in the coming sessions. For individuals exchanging small amounts, the parallel market may offer quicker access to cash dollars, while businesses with approved documentation are expected to source foreign exchange through the official banking and NFEM channels. items.title: La Russie prépare-t-elle une opération sous faux drapeau sur le territoire de l’OTAN ?
items.description: Jeudi, 6 août, le ministre lituanien de la Défense, Robertas Kaunas, a rendu publique une évaluation du renseignement militaire selon laquelle Moscou envisagerait d'utiliser des drones ukrainiens capturés pour mener une attaque contre les pays baltes sous la forme d'une opération sous faux drapeau visant des infrastructures critiques. Kaunas décrit ces conclusions comme un scénario réaliste Lithuania says Russia could use Ukrainian drones against Baltic region », Reuters , 6 août 2026.'> 1 . Dans le même temps, Robertas Kaunas ajoute qu'il n'existe actuellement aucune indication que la Russie ait pris la décision de passer à l'acte, ni qu'une attaque soit imminente, même si Moscou serait en possession de drones ukrainiens. Selon le scénario décrit par Vilnius, Moscou pourrait croire que les États baltes ont ouvert leur espace aérien aux drones ukrainiens pour frapper la Russie. Si un drone ukrainien était reconditionné et lancé contre une infrastructure balte, l'origine réelle de l'attaque pourrait être dissimulée et toute implication dans une frappe sur le territoire de l'OTAN niée. La Lituanie envisage actuellement d'implanter une usine de drones ukrainiens sur son territoire. Bien que le pays soit l'un des principaux soutiens de Kiev, Kaunas a déclaré qu'il n'avait pas autorisé l'Ukraine à utiliser son espace aérien pour mener des attaques contre la Russie. Moscou n’a pas encore répondu à ces déclarations, mais en juillet, le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, avait qualifié les avertissements des pays baltes de tactiques de peur destinées à justifier « la militarisation contre la Russie ». Il ne s'agit pas d'une déclaration isolée. Le média polonais Onet rapportait le 30 juin que Moscou pourrait préparer une provocation militaire limitée contre la Pologne, les États-Unis ayant averti Varsovie de nouveaux plans russes visant le flanc est de l'OTAN. Des déclarations similaires sur une possible attaque russe sous faux drapeau avaient également été faites par le ministre polonais des Affaires étrangères, Radek Sikorski Poland's deputy prime minister says Russia could launch a « false flag operation » to justify an attack on a NATO state », CBS News , 26 juin 2026.'> 2 . Dans un entretien avec le Financial Times en avril, Donald Tusk déclarait que la Russie pourrait attaquer un pays membre de l’OTAN « d’ici quelques mois » Polish PM questions whether US is ‘loyal’ to Europe’s defence », Financial Times , 24 avril 2026.'> 3 . Le 3 juillet, il a indiqué que les mois à venir pourraient être critiques, avec des inquiétudes particulières concernant les pays baltes Polish PM warns critical months ahead in face of Russian threat », BBC , 3 juillet 2026.'> 4 . Le président lituanien Nausėda évoquait des informations sur des opérations limitées visant les infrastructures critiques Lithuania says Russia is planning attacks on infrastructure », Reuters , 15 juillet 2026.'> 5 . Son homologue letton Rinkēvičs jugeait lui aussi les douze prochains mois décisifs The coming months will be crucial for Baltic security, Rinkēvičs warns », Baltic News Network , 15 juillet 2026.'> 6 . Cette prise de parole intervient alors qu'un drone chargé d'explosifs a été découvert le jour précédent à proximité d'un avion cargo ukrainien, à l'aéroport de Leipzig, en Allemagne. Si le ministre allemand de l'Intérieur, Dobrindt, évoque un scénario d'attaque hybride, il ne désigne aucun responsable. items.title: Fuel pricing norm broken as market turns ‘radically volatile’ – COMAC CEO
items.description: The CEO of the Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies (COMAC), Dr Riverson Oppong, says Ghana’s fuel market has entered an unusually volatile phase, forcing oil marketing companies (OMCs) to respond in ways rarely seen under the country’s pricing system. His comments come as the government rolls out a ¢ 2-per-litre cushioning on diesel after another round of increases in petroleum prices, aimed at easing the burden on consumers and businesses. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Dr Oppong said recent developments in the global oil market, triggered by the conflict involving the United States and Iran, have disrupted the normal fuel pricing pattern. “Let me say we are seeing the changes in the market. Things are not easy, and my members are really adhering to it.” He recalled that when the conflict began, OMCs initially resisted increasing pump prices even as bulk distribution companies faced rising costs. “When this US-Iran war started, I gave this analysis. The first time we started, we were just three days in a pricing window. No single OMC added a pesewa, even though some BDCs were increasing prices. No single OMC added prices.” According to him, the market has since behaved in a way not witnessed for a long time. “This is the first time in a long time that we’ve seen OMCs changing prices when we are within a window, and it tells you how probably tight first of all, and how radically volatile the market has been.” Dr Oppong pointed to the sharp swings in global crude oil prices as evidence of the uncertainty confronting the industry. “See how we jumped to $100 per barrel, and now we are back to the $70s.” He questioned why consumers have not seen pump prices fall at the same pace as international oil prices. “So you ask a very simple and smart question that why is it that when everything else is now coming down, we’re not seeing that in the market just as we saw it going up?” The COMAC CEO also raised concerns about whether Ghana’s current pricing framework remains suitable under such volatile conditions. “This is more reason why I am asking NPA a very simple question. Going to spot pricing daily changes is that an option that we want to go, or that two weeks window…” He said the cost of importing fuel remains elevated despite the drop in crude oil prices because traders continue to face high premiums and rising logistics costs. “As Dr. Kweku Ofori said, the premiums are high, they are doubled in the market today due to freight costs and even insurance. “I don’t talk about the demurrage because that’s not part of my business. That’s the BDC side. But I know that the insurance globally, as we all know, because of this war, has increased.”

items.title: Ghana’s digital trust debate needs better performance evidence
items.description: Trust has become a central question in Ghana’s digital economy. As more payments, purchases and financial decisions move onto apps, a consumer must decide whether a platform is legitimate, whether it performs reliably and what happens when something goes wrong. Those are related questions, but they are not the same. A trust seal can help verify a business. A regulator’s register can confirm formal status. Customer reviews can reveal patterns in service. None of those sources, by itself, proves the whole case. The Bank of Ghana’s publication of its 2024 fraud report has brought renewed attention to attempted and successful fraud across banks, specialised deposit-taking institutions and payment service providers. The policy response should include stronger controls and consumer education. It should also improve the quality of the evidence consumers see when comparing digital services. Verification is the first layer Before judging performance, a consumer needs to know who operates the service. The website and app should identify the legal entity, relevant registration or licence, physical and digital contact points, and the regulator or complaint body with jurisdiction. This is where registers and trust seals are valuable. They reduce the risk that a consumer mistakes an anonymous seller or impersonation page for an established business. They also give legitimate companies a verifiable way to distinguish themselves. Verification should be presented with an “as of” date. Legal status, ownership and permissions can change. A badge without a source and date may remain visible after the evidence behind it has expired. Performance requires different evidence A verified business can still have outages, unclear fees, slow dispute handling or poor customer support. Those issues require operational and consumer-experience evidence. A transparent rating should separate at least four layers: formal standing, product terms, operational signals and aggregated customer experience. Combining them can be useful, but the user should be able to see the components and understand which source supports each conclusion. For example, a regulator’s register can establish that an entity is authorised for a defined activity. It does not prove that an app is easy to use. Customer reviews can identify recurring service problems. They cannot establish that a company is solvent. A privacy notice can show what the business promises to do with data. It does not prove that every internal process follows the notice. Star averages need context Consumers often see a star average before they see the company name. The number is useful only when its context is visible. How many reviews produced the score? Were they collected recently? Can the platform identify verified transactions? How does it treat incentives, suspicious activity and negative feedback? Are complaints concentrated around one event or spread over time? An average without those details can reward the company with the strongest review campaign rather than the strongest service. The goal is not to reject public reviews, but to treat them as one evidence source with known limitations. Confidence should be shown beside the score Two services can receive similar scores from very different evidence. One may have complete regulatory records, current terms and thousands of recent reviews. Another may have a small sample and unclear ownership. A single score hides that difference. A confidence label makes it visible. The score tells consumers what the available evidence suggests; confidence tells them how complete, current and independent that evidence is. When important evidence is missing, the responsible response is to lower confidence or withhold a score. Filling the gap with an estimate makes a table look complete while transferring hidden uncertainty to the consumer. The IndexFair methodology provides one model for publishing source categories, evidence limits and the rules used to produce a consumer-brand rating. Ghanaian platforms do not need to adopt the same formula. They can adopt the same principle: every summary should have a visible route back to its evidence. Complaint handling belongs inside the rating A digital service is tested most clearly when something fails. The quality of complaint handling should therefore be part of the public record, not an afterthought. Useful indicators include whether the business publishes a complaint channel, acknowledges submissions, provides a reference number, states an escalation path and records the time to resolution. Aggregate outcomes can be reported without exposing personal information. The rating platform also needs its own correction route. A consumer should be able to submit evidence that a term or status is outdated. A company should be able to challenge a factual error without paying for access or receiving control over the conclusion. Material corrections should remain visible in a changelog. Commercial influence should stop at a public line Ratings and comparison services cost money to operate. Advertising, referrals and analytics can finance the work. Consumers should not have to guess whether those relationships can change a score. A platform should state whether payment can secure inclusion, improve placement, preview a result or suppress criticism. If commercial clients are also rated, the relationship should be disclosed and the editorial boundary should be enforced through documented controls. From trust signals to trust infrastructure Ghana does not lack trust signals. It has official registers, regulatory reporting, industry initiatives and a growing body of consumer experience. The opportunity is to connect those sources without pretending they are interchangeable. A strong public rating record would identify the entity, show the relevant formal status, summarise measurable product terms, aggregate reviews with clear denominators, publish a confidence label and preserve corrections. That system would not ask consumers to trust a new badge. It would give them a structured way to inspect why the badge exists, where the evidence is weak and how the conclusion can be challenged. In a digital economy, that is the difference between marketing trust and building trust infrastructure. By: Zack Lowy

items.title: Paul Afoko vows to reunite NPP and lead party back to power in 2028
items.description: Former National Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Paul Awentami Afoko, has pledged to lead the party back to government in the 2028 general election if he is re-elected as National Chairman. Mr Afoko expressed confidence that the NPP could regain the trust of Ghanaians, insisting that the party remained capable of returning to power through unity, discipline and a strengthened grassroots structure. Speaking in an interview Akoma in Kumasi on Thursday, August 6, Mr Afoko said his decision to seek a return as National Chairman followed extensive consultations with party elders, former and current national executives, Members of Parliament, regional executives, as well as youth, women and grassroots groups across the country. According to him, the engagements revealed widespread concern about the party’s current state but also a strong belief that it could overcome its challenges under purposeful leadership. Mr Afoko said his campaign would be anchored on what he described as the “Three Rs” — Reunite, Rebuild and Recapture. He explained that reuniting the party would involve healing divisions, restoring trust and promoting inclusiveness, while rebuilding would focus on strengthening party structures, empowering grassroots members and ensuring all organs of the party function effectively. Speaking during the interview, Mr Afoko said these measures would position the NPP to recapture political power by restoring public confidence and presenting the party as a united, disciplined and credible alternative ready to govern. He also appealed to delegates to support his candidature, promising transparent, inclusive and selfless leadership that would place the interests of the party above personal ambition. He further urged members to uphold the values of sacrifice, commitment and service, stressing that unity remained the surest path to returning the NPP to government.

items.title: YEA to expand youth employment opportunities in Western North – Malik Basintale
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Youth Employment Agency (YEA), Malik Basintale, has reaffirmed the Agency’s commitment to expanding employment opportunities for young people across Ghana, with particular attention to the Western North Region. Mr Basintale gave the assurance on Wednesday, August 6, during a courtesy call on the Western North Regional Minister, Wilbert Petty Brentum, at the Regional Coordinating Council ahead of a staff durbar in the region. Welcoming the YEA delegation, Mr Brentum described Western North as one of Ghana’s most peaceful and hospitable regions. He noted that the youth remain central to President John Dramani Mahama’s Reset Agenda and stressed that the region’s development depends on sustained investment in the skills, innovation and potential of its young people. The Regional Minister appealed to the YEA to prioritise Western North in the implementation of its employment and empowerment programmes. He also called on Mr Basintale and his team to support the region’s representative in the 2026 Ghana’s Most Beautiful competition. Responding, Mr Basintale thanked the Regional Minister and the people of Western North for the warm reception, reaffirming the Agency’s resolve to ensure that employment opportunities are available to young people across the country, regardless of their location. He disclosed that the YEA has so far deployed more than 9,000 young people under its nationwide sanitation module, trained 30,000 beneficiaries through various skills development programmes, including about 800 from the Western North Region, and facilitated more than 1,800 youth employment opportunities in the region. Mr Basintale also revealed that over 600 Ghanaian youth have benefited from international exchange programmes, with more opportunities expected to be introduced in the coming months. He said the visit was aimed not only at paying a courtesy call on the Regional Minister but also at strengthening collaboration with the Regional Coordinating Council to create sustainable jobs and expand opportunities for the youth in the Western North Region.

items.title: UNSC condemns Swat suicide blast after Pakistan sounds alarm on Afghan terrorist havens
items.description: UNITED NATIONS: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) on Thursday strongly condemned the suicide bombing in Swat last week, calling it a “heinous and cowardly” terrorist attack after Pakistan warned the body that multiple terrorist groups continue to operate from safe havens inside Afghanistan. In a press statement issued by the Office of the UN secretary general’s spokesperson, the council said it condemned “in the strongest terms” the “heinous and cowardly” suicide attack outside the police station in Swat’s Kabal on Aug 2. “This reprehensible act of terrorism resulted in the grievous loss of at least 16 Pakistani nationals, mostly civilians, and injuries to dozens of others. Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) has claimed responsibility for this terrorist attack,” it added. The UNSC also expressed solidarity with Pakistan, saying, “The members of the Security Council express their deepest sympathy and condolences to the families of the victims and to the government and the people of Pakistan, and wish a speedy and full recovery to those who were injured.” The statement reaffirmed the international body’s longstanding position that terrorism “in all its forms and manifestations constitutes one of the most serious threats to international peace and security”. It further stressed the importance of bringing those responsible to justice, declaring: “The members of the council underlined the need to hold perpetrators, organisers, financiers and sponsors of these reprehensible acts of terrorism accountable and bring them to justice.” They urged all UN member states, in accordance with their obligations under international law and relevant UNSC resolutions, to cooperate actively with the government of Pakistan in this regard. The council also reiterated that “any acts of terrorism are criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, wherever, whenever and by whomsoever committed” and reaffirmed that all countries must combat terrorism in accordance with the UN Charter and international law, including international human rights, refugee and humanitarian law. Earlier this week, Pakistan told a UNSC meeting that several terrorist organisations continue to operate from sanctuaries inside Afghanistan, posing an increasing threat to regional and international security. Addressing a briefing on threats to international peace and security caused by terrorism, Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar, said the country continued to face a grave terrorist threat emanating from across its western border. He identified the banned TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its Majeed Brigade, the Islamic State Khorasan (IS-K) and its affiliates, the East Turkistan Islamic Movement (ETIM), and Al Qaeda affiliates as groups that, according to Pakistan, maintain safe havens inside Afghanistan. Pakistan urged the international community to ensure that Afghan territory is not used by terrorist organisations to launch attacks against neighbouring countries and called for stronger international cooperation against cross-border terrorism. The developments also followed the fourth US-Pakistan Counterterrorism Dialogue held in Washington on Tuesday, where officials from both countries reaffirmed their commitment to combating terrorist organisations.

items.title: NPP had no intention of disrespecting helicopter crash victims with protest – Salam Mustapha
items.description: The National Youth Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Salam Mustapha, has rejected suggestions that the party’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration was disrespectful to the memory of the eight people who died in the August 6, 2025, military helicopter crash. He said the decision to hold the protest on the same day as the national inter-faith memorial service was based on the party’s internal activities calendar and was not intended to undermine the significance of the commemoration. Mr Mustapha explained that the NPP had already factored in its constituency and upcoming regional elections when selecting a date for the demonstration and was unaware of the government’s programme at the time. The protest took place in Accra on Thursday, August 6, with the NPP accusing the government of selective justice, political persecution and the misuse of state institutions. Some members of the public criticised the timing of the demonstration because it coincided with a memorial service attended by government officials, religious leaders and the families of the crash victims. Speaking on Citi FM on Thursday, August 6, Mr Mustapha maintained that the party held the victims in the highest regard and believed they would have supported the democratic ideals underpinning the protest. “We have absolute respect for the memory of our gallant men who died. Absolute respect. One of them was a personal friend, the Honourable Murtala. Very personal. “When we were discussing this matter, we were not in the know as to what programme the government had. So we were looking at our calendar as far as our activities are concerned. “Knowing the repertoire of men who were involved, they would identify with the issues we demonstrated today. These were people who believed in the tenets of democracy,” he said. The helicopter crash claimed the lives of Defence Minister Dr Edward Kofi Omane Boamah; Minister for Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation Dr Ibrahim Murtala Muhammed; Acting Deputy National Security Coordinator Alhaji Muniru Mohammed; former Ashanti Regional Minister Dr Samuel Sarpong; former NDC parliamentary candidate Samuel Aboagye; Squadron Leader Peter Bafemi Anala; Flying Officer Manaen Twum Ampadu; and Flight Sergeant Ernest Addo Mensah.

items.title: 12 suspected illegal miners remanded over Bosomtwe Forest Reserve operation
items.description: Twelve suspected illegal miners have been remanded into police custody after they were arrested during a two-day operation against illegal mining in the Bosomtwe Range Forest Reserve in the Ashanti Region. The operation, conducted by the Bekwai Forest District of the Forestry Commission on July 31 and August 1, targeted illegal mining activities within Compartments 1, 10 and 12 of the protected forest reserve. During the exercise, the enforcement team immobilised an excavator and seized several items allegedly used for illegal mining, including a tricycle, seven changfan machines, 21 water pumping machines, two power plants, two generators and an air blower. The suspects — Abu Naa, Adakwa Mathew, John Tibootey, Nurudeen Issah, Henry Peter, Ruth Agbenyo, Anthony Amadi, Sesi Mclean, Benjamin Owusu, Richard Atta, Sumaila Mohammed and Abel Nti — were subsequently arraigned before the Bekwai Circuit Court. Presiding over the case, His Honour Isaac Apeatu remanded the accused persons into police custody. They are expected to reappear before the court on August 11 and 12, 2026. The Forestry Commission also disclosed that one Abena Ahenkan, believed to be the alleged leader of one of the illegal mining groups, escaped during the operation and is currently being sought by the authorities. The Commission reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding Ghana’s forest reserves from illegal mining, stressing that enforcement operations would continue to target individuals whose activities threaten the country’s forests and other natural resources.

Madam Jantuah said the Minority Leader’s remarks were not only disrespectful to her but also to President John Dramani Mahama, who had delegated her to receive the petition on his behalf. Speaking on Asempa FM’s Ekosii Sen, she said the President had asked her to stand in for him because he and other government officials were attending events marking the first anniversary of the helicopter crash that claimed the lives of several national figures. “Everyone was at the one-year anniversary of the helicopter crash victims, so the President suggested I go and receive the petition. They gave me a call time of 11 a.m., but they arrived around 1 p.m.,” she said. According to her, some members of the NPP delegation initially refused to present the petition after realising she had been delegated to receive it. “I watched from afar as they protested that they wouldn’t hand over the petition to me. I didn’t react because I was there in the stead of the President,” she stated. Nana Yaa Jantuah alleged that the NPP leaders held internal discussions before deciding not to hand over the petition. She expressed disappointment over what she described as the Minority Leader’s conduct, saying he had no justification for speaking to her in that manner. “I am old enough to be your mother. Afenyo-Markin is a small boy in my eyes. Who is he to disrespect me? He should never try that again,” she said.

items.title: 10 terrorists killed in 2 separate operations in KP: ISPR
items.description: The military’s media affairs wing said on Friday that 10 terrorists were killed in two separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa a day earlier. Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the terrorists belonged to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khwarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. It said that in the first encounter, a group of terrorists attempted to attack security forces’ checkposts in Azam Warsak area in South Waziristan. “The attempt was effectively thwarted by own troops. During ensuing fire exchange, eight khwarij were sent to hell through effective and precise engagements by own troops,” it said. “In another encounter that took place in Dir district, own troops successfully neutralised two more khwarij ,” it added. ISPR said that weapons and ammunition were also seized from killed terrorists, who remained “actively involved in numerous terrorist activities in the area”. It said sanitisation operations were being conducted to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area, adding that the counterterrorism campaign would continue at full pace to wipe out “the menace of foreign sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”. President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the country’s security forces for eliminating the terrorists and commended their professionalism in thwarting the attack in Azam Warsak. “The nation stands with its brave security forces and law enforcement agencies and views their sacrifices against terrorism with utmost appreciation,” he said. “The nefarious designs of terrorist elements active under Indian sponsorship will be thwarted at any cost,” he added. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also praised security forces for the successful operations. “The nefarious designs of elements spreading terrorism under Indian patronage will be thwarted at any cost. The government and the entire nation stand with the security forces in the war against terrorism,” he asserted. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , an Islamabad-based think tank, violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July, making it the deadliest month of 2026, with 112 security personnel among 205 people killed.

items.title: Latin America’s new imaginaries
items.description: This week, Mark Leonard is joined by Adriana Abdenur, a Brazilian policy expert and co-president of the Global Fund for a New Economy, and Jorge Castañeda, former foreign minister of Mexico and professor at Sciences Po, to explore debates about development and ideas of strategic autonomy across Latin America. Jorge explains why China’s role is varied across the region, arguing that Mexico and much of Central America remain deeply constrained by their economic ties to the US. Adriana discusses Brazil’s long tradition of strategic autonomy, describing how policymakers engage with China as both an economic partner and a source of ideas on development, technology and global governance. Together, Mark, Adriana and Jorge explore how intensifying US-China competition is reshaping the region’s choices. Can Latin American countries balance relations with both powers? Is China a model, a market or simply another partner in a multipolar world? And what does strategic autonomy look like in an increasingly coercive geopolitical environment? This podcast episode was recorded on July 31st 2026. Bookshelf Latin American Foreign Policies in the New World Order: The Active Non-Alignment Option , by Carlos Ominami, Jorge Heine and Carlos Fortín Manifesto Antropófago (Cannibal Manifesto) , by Oswald de Andrade Source

items.title: GACL bars two Port Health officers over alleged Yellow Fever Card extortion
items.description: The Ghana Airports Company Limited (GACL) has barred two Port Health officers from working at Accra International Airport and all other airports under its management after they were found to have overcharged a passenger for a Yellow Fever Card. According to GACL, the officers, who were stationed at Terminal 3 of Accra International Airport, charged a foreign passport holder US$40 for a Yellow Fever Card on August 5 instead of the approved fee of US$20. In a statement issued on Thursday, August 6, the company said the officers had their airport identification cards withdrawn and deactivated with immediate effect. “Their ID cards to operate in the terminal have been withdrawn and deactivated. As of Thursday, 6th August 2026, the two officers are no longer permitted to work at Accra International Airport or any other GACL-operated airport,” the statement said. The sanctions come barely a day after GACL announced a raft of measures to clamp down on extortion at the country’s airports. These include a mystery shopping programme, a “name and shame” policy, stricter disciplinary measures and a dedicated hotline for passengers to report misconduct. The company also disclosed that the Ghana Immigration Service had transferred an immigration officer captured in a viral video allegedly demanding money from a traveller for “breakfast”. Reaffirming its zero-tolerance stance on extortion, GACL said surveillance and enforcement would be intensified across all airports under its management and urged passengers to report incidents through its hotline. “Everyone is being watched,” the company warned, encouraging travellers to “Spot it. Record it. Report it.”

items.title: NPP vows to defend members against alleged political persecution
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says it will defend its members against what it alleges is political persecution by the Government. The party said it would oppose what it described as attempts to intimidate or silence members of the political opposition. Mr Salam Mustapha, National Youth Organiser of the NPP, said this in an interview with journalists during the party’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration in Accra on Thursday. He alleged that the Government was using state institutions to target members of the opposition instead of addressing the country’s economic challenges. “We do not have a problem with state institutions working and calling people to account for their stewardship, but we have a problem with persecution. “As a political entity, we will defend our members. We will not allow this Government to have its way in cowing our members into submission,” he said. The demonstration was organised by the NPP to highlight what the party described as concerns over governance, constitutional rights and the functioning of democratic institutions. Mr Mustapha also alleged that the removal of the immediate former Chief Justice had undermined the independence of the Judiciary and created fear within the justice system. He said political activists should not be targeted for their views and argued that failure to challenge such actions could expose other groups, including the media, to similar treatment. “Strange things are happening to our democracy,” he said. “We all have a responsibility to raise our voices because Ghana was not sold to any political party. Ghanaians voted with the expectation that food prices, fuel prices and the cost of living would come down, not for political opponents to be persecuted,” he added. Mr Mustapha said the NPP would continue to oppose what he described as tyranny, dictatorship and demagoguery. Mr Faisal Ibrahim Cisse, NPP Chairman for the Klottey Korle Constituency, also expressed concern over what he described as increasing arrests of people over comments made on social media and other public platforms. He alleged that some citizens had been detained without due process and said freedom of expression was guaranteed under the Constitution. Mr Cisse said people who believed they had been defamed could seek redress through civil proceedings instead of criminal arrests. He urged the Government to uphold democratic principles and ensure that the law was applied impartially, irrespective of the political affiliation of those involved.

items.title: Government urged to tolerate dissent
items.description: Dennis Miracles Aboagye, Spokesperson for Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has called on the Government to demonstrate greater tolerance for dissenting opinions, warning that attempts to intimidate critics undermine Ghana’s democratic credentials. He said democracy thrived on the free exchange of ideas and differing viewpoints, stressing that a political environment in which citizens feared speaking openly could not be described as democratic. Mr Aboagye made the remarks in Accra ahead of the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration scheduled for Thursday. The protest, according to the Party, was intended to draw national attention to concerns over alleged political persecution, selective justice, abuse of state institutions and what it considers growing intimidation of opposition members. Mr Aboagye expressed concern over what he described as a growing culture of fear among citizens, alleging that critics of the Government increasingly felt vulnerable to intimidation and persecution. “If you are in government and people are afraid to speak, then what becomes of democracy?” he questioned, adding that the power of the State could easily be used to target individuals once they were perceived as opponents. Mr Aboagye said although he had not personally suffered any such treatment, many Ghanaians, particularly ordinary citizens in remote communities, had allegedly been subjected to what he described as unfair actions by the security and judicial systems. He cited the case of a young woman who, according to him, had been remanded into custody under bail conditions she could not meet, arguing that such incidents reflected a troubling trend within the justice delivery system. Mr Aboagye said he had, on behalf of his group, the People’s Forum, written to the Chief Justice some weeks ago to raise concerns about what he described as the increasing confidence of security agencies in securing favourable outcomes from the courts. He alleged that some security agencies had become convinced that cases they brought before the courts would proceed without sufficient judicial scrutiny. Mr Aboagye argued that stronger judicial oversight would serve as an effective check against any abuse of power by law enforcement agencies. “The security agencies think they are even doing you a favour by taking you to court because, in their view, the courts will make matters worse,” he claimed. Mr Aboagye also criticised what he described as the criminalisation of insults, saying the incarceration of citizens solely for making insulting remarks was inconsistent with democratic governance and constitutional freedoms. He maintained that while offensive language should not be encouraged, the appropriate response should be public education rather than imprisonment. Mr Aboagye called on institutions such as the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) to intensify civic education to help citizens understand the distinction between protected speech, insults and criminal threats, as well as the legal limits of free expression. He also questioned the arrest of individuals over comments made on social media platforms, including TikTok, saying many users lacked adequate understanding of the legal boundaries governing online expression. Mr Aboagye urged the Government to prioritise education and engagement instead of using what he described as intimidation to discourage public criticism. “Our responsibility should be to educate citizens on how to express themselves within the confines of the law, not to silence them through fear,” he said.

items.title: Helicopter crash: Religious leaders call for service, sacrifice to honour fallen heroes
items.description: Religious leaders have urged Ghanaians to uphold the values of service, faith and sacrifice demonstrated by eight public officials who died in a military helicopter crash. They said the best way to honour the memory of the victims was to emulate their commitment to duty and contribute to national development and peace. The call was made during the National Interfaith Memorial Service for the “Departed 8” held in Accra on Thursday, one year after the Ghana Air Force helicopter crash that claimed their lives. The service, held on the theme: “Lives of Service, Legacies of Sacrifice,” brought together government officials, security chiefs, religious leaders, traditional authorities, families of the deceased and members of the public to commemorate the victims. Delivering the Christian sermon, Brigadier General Benjamin Godson Kumi-Woode, Director General of Religious Affairs of the Ghana Armed Forces, said the lives of people who served with faith and commitment provided examples for future generations. Citing Hebrews 11:4, he said although Abel died thousands of years ago, his life of faith continued to “speak” through the testimony of his righteous deeds. Brig. Gen. Kumi-Woode said the legacy of the fallen officials should remind Ghanaians that true greatness was measured by service, humility and obedience to God rather than material possessions or public recognition. He said the victims demonstrated loyalty, professionalism, patriotism and dedication to duty, with some making the ultimate sacrifice while serving the nation. “Their legacy should inspire us to serve the nation with integrity and dedication in our respective fields. Let’s focus on the values instead of material possessions because while wealth fades, a life of faith, honesty and selfless service continue to influence generations,” he said. Brig. Gen. Kumi-Woode prayed for eternal peace for the departed, strength for their families and continued unity, stability and peace for the country. The eight victims were Dr Edward Kofi Omane Boamah, Minister for Defence; Dr Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed, Member of Parliament for Tamale Central and Minister for Environment, Science and Technology; Alhaji Muniru Mohammed Limuna, Acting Deputy National Security Coordinator; and Dr Samuel Sarpong, Vice Chairman of the National Democratic Congress. The others were Samuel Aboagye, Deputy Director-General of the National Disaster Management Organisation; Wing Commander Peter Bafemi Anala; Flight Lieutenant Manaen Twum Ampadu; and Flight Sergeant Ernest Addo Mensah of the Ghana Air Force. Family representatives paid tribute to their relatives, recalling their contributions to public service and describing the past year as a period marked by grief, reflection and reliance on faith. “While the past year has been marked by deep grief and loss, God has sustained us with strength, comfort, and hope. Though we deeply miss our beloved fathers, husbands, sons, and brothers, we remain grateful for the lives they lived, the service they rendered to Ghana, and the enduring legacies they left behind,” said Charles Ohene Nti,who spoke on behalf of the family of the late Dr Omane Boamah, said: Percy Anala, representing the family of Wing Commander Peter Bafemi Anala, said: “The loss of our beloved Peter Bafemi Anala is profoundly painful. His absence can never be truly and everyday reminds us of the huge void he leaves.” “I have lost count of the number of times I have pulled out my phone to share a picture with him, only to remember that I will not get a response. It has been hard, but it is well. I stand here today grateful for my faith in God. It would have been an even scarier nightmare without God,” Mrs Ampadu said on behalf of the family of Flight Lieutenant Manaen Twum Ampadu. Mercy Amoah, speaking on behalf of the family of Flight Sergeant Ernest Addo Mensah, said: “For us, it was not only the loss of a husband, son or brother, but a painful separation from a force that stood by and with us through every season of our lives…we still remember, still mourn…” The service was attended by President John Dramani Mahama, Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, Dr Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff, ministers of state, Members of Parliament, heads of security services, members of the Judiciary, diplomatic representatives, traditional leaders, religious leaders and other dignitaries. The Ghana Air Force Harbin Z-9 helicopter crashed on August 6, 2025, near Sikaman in the Adansi Akrofuom District of the Ashanti Region while carrying officials from Accra to Obuasi for an official assignment linked to efforts against illegal mining. All eight occupants died in the crash, which led to three days of national mourning, a state funeral and an official investigation into the cause of the accident.
